{"content": "1|# Issue #889
2|# title: [improve] tickets.priority accepts medium/high in the DB but no report reads them - maintenance:generate-due writes 'medium' nightly and those tickets fall outside every priority bucket
3|# author: haileen7
4|# created: 2026-10-09T01:30:13Z
5|# url: https://github.com/asgarimehdi/h-dashboard/issues/889
6|# labels: []
7|
8|## Problem
9|
10|The `tickets.priority` column carries **five** accepted values at the database level, but only **three** of them are understood by any application code. Two values — `medium` and `high` — are accepted by the DB, offered by one UI filter, and read by **no** bucket, aggregation, or label map anywhere in the app.
11|
12|Where the divergence comes from:
13|
14|| Layer | Values accepted | Source |
15||---|---|---|
16|| DB CHECK constraint | `urgent`, `high`, `normal`, `medium`, `low` | `database/migrations/2026_07_28_000001_add_medium_priority_to_tickets_table.php:21` |
17|| Livewire create form | `low`, `normal`, `urgent` | `resources/views/livewire/tickets/⚡create.blade.php:232-235` |
18|| API create/update rules | `low`, `normal`, `urgent` | `app/Http/Controllers/Api/TicketController.php:68`, `:101` |
19|| API index filter rule | `low`, `normal`, `urgent` | `app/Http/Controllers/Api/TicketController.php:20` |
20|| Map dashboard filter | `urgent`, `high`, `normal`, `medium`, `low` | `resources/views/livewire/map/map-dashboard.blade.php:152-156` |
21|| Dashboard priority tiles | `urgent`, `normal`, `low` only | `resources/views/livewire/dashboard.blade.php:197-199` |
22|| Advanced report breakdown | `urgent`, `normal`, `low` only | `resources/views/livewire/reports/advanced.blade.php:187-189` |
23|| Calendar event colours | `urgent`, `normal`, `low` only | `resources/views/livewire/todo/todo.blade.php:98` |
24|| **Generated by a scheduled command** | **`medium`** | **`app/Console/Commands/GenerateDueMaintenance.php:70`** |
25|
26|The database-level expansion was deliberate — the migration exists specifically to allow `medium` and `high`. But the application was never updated to match, so those two values fall into a hole: stored, filterable, and counted in no chart.
27|
28|**One value is written by a scheduled job that runs unattended**, so this is not only a theoretical inconsistency:
29|
30|```php
31|// app/Console/Commands/GenerateDueMaintenance.php:66-72
32|$ticket = Ticket::create([
33|    'ticket_code' => 'T-'.strtoupper(Str::random(8)),
34|    'subject' => $schedule->title,
35|    'content' => 'Generated from maintenance schedule #'.$schedule->id,
36|    'status' => 'created',
37|    'priority' => 'medium',   // ← outside every app-level rule
38|    'unit_id' => $schedule->unit_id,
39|]);
40|```
41|
42|## Impact
43|
44|Every ticket generated from a maintenance schedule is invisible to the priority reporting it is supposed to appear in. Verified against the live database (probe run inside a transaction, then rolled back):
45|
46|```
47|== dashboard priority buckets ==           (dashboard.blade.php:197-200, same unit scope)
48|urgent=0 normal=0 low=0  |  SUM(shown)=0  medium_bucket=1 high_bucket=1  offenum_open=2
49|```
50|
51|The two off-enum tickets are open (`created`) but contribute **zero** to the sum of the three tiles the dashboard renders. Concretely:
52|
53|- **Dashboard tiles** (`dashboard.blade.php:562-570`) — `urgent + normal + low` no longer equals the number of open tickets. A maintenance-generated ticket makes the numbers disagree with each other and with the "open tickets" tile at `:115`.
54|- **Advanced report** (`reports/advanced.blade.php:187-189`) — same three buckets, same omission, so the breakdown silently under-reports.
55|- **Calendar** (`todo/todo.blade.php:98`) — `$priorityColors[$ticket->priority] ?? '#f59e0b'` falls back to amber (the *normal* colour) for a `medium` ticket, so on the calendar it is visually indistinguishable from `normal` despite being a distinct value.
56|- **API inconsistency** — `POST /api/tickets` rejects `medium`/`high` with a 422, but a maintenance-generated ticket already carries `medium` in the database. A client that reads the ticket back and then PUTs it back fails validation on a value the system itself created.
57|
58|The `medium` value is currently invisible in the data because maintenance generation has not yet produced one in this database (`tickets` currently holds only `low`=14, `normal`=19, `urgent`=17). This is a latent defect that fires as soon as the first maintenance schedule becomes due — and #876 separately reports that command failing on unit-less schedules, so the two interact.
59|
60|## Proposed action
61|
62|Decide the canonical priority vocabulary, then make every layer agree. The smallest coherent option:
63|
64|1. **Narrow the write path.** Change `GenerateDueMaintenance.php:70` from `'medium'` to `'normal'` so the only unattended writer produces a value every aggregation understands. This alone removes the auto-generated blind spot.
65|2. **Align the map dashboard filter** (`map-dashboard.blade.php:152-156`) with the three values the rest of the app uses, so the filter cannot select a bucket that reports nothing.

Either give it a bucket alongside `urgent`, or drop it from the CHECK constraint in a new migration. Leaving it in place means the schema permanently permits rows no report can see.
67|4. **Add a guard.** The three aggregation sites (`dashboard.blade.php:197-199`, `reports/advanced.blade.php:187-189`, `todo/todo.blade.php:98`) hardcode their bucket lists independently, which is how they drifted. The same verification shows the same scope returning 2 / 3 / 0 open tickets under the three different "open" definitions in use. {"content": "1|# Issue #934
2|# title: [improve] the vendored MaryUI POST /mary/upload writes an unvalidated file to a client-chosen disk - any authenticated user (viewer included) can drop arbitrary content on a web-served disk, and the route is registered by the package, not by this app
3|# author: haileen7
4|# created: 2026-10-10T03:32:41Z
5|# url: https://github.com/asgarimehdi/h-dashboard/issues/934
6|# labels: []
7|
8|[improve] the vendored MaryUI POST /mary/upload writes an unvalidated file to a client-chosen disk - any authenticated user (viewer included) can drop arbitrary content on a web-served disk, and the route is registered by the package, not by this app
9|
10|## Problem
11|
12|`POST /mary/upload` is live in this application and is registered **by the MaryUI package**, not by `routes/web.php`. Its handler does no validation at all, and takes both the disk and the destination folder from the request body.
13|
14|`vendor/robsontenorio/mary/routes/web.php:17-25`:
15|
16|```php
17|Route::middleware(['web', 'auth'])->prefix(config('mary.route_prefix'))->post('/mary/upload', function (Request $request) {
18|    $disk = $request->disk ?? 'public';
19|    $folder = $request->folder ?? 'editor';
20|
21|    $file = Storage::disk($disk)->put($folder, $request->file('file'), 'public');
22|    $url = Storage::disk($disk)->url($file);
23|
24|    return ['location' => $url];
25|})->name('mary.upload');
26|```
27|
28|There is no `$request->validate()` on this closure. No `mimes:`, no `max:`, no `image` rule. Three facts make it reachable in this deployment:
29|
30|1. **The route is registered.** `php artisan route:list` reports it live:
31|   ```
32|   POST   mary/upload   mary.upload   Closure
33|          middleware: ["web","Illuminate\Auth\Middleware\Authenticate"]
34|   ```
35|   `config/mary.php:34` sets `route_prefix` to `''`, so it sits at the app root rather than behind a namespaced prefix. It is loaded unconditionally by `MaryServiceProvider::boot()` via `$this->loadRoutesFrom(__DIR__.'/../routes/web.php')` (`vendor/robsontenorio/mary/src/MaryServiceProvider.php:91`) — there is no app-side toggle that removes it.
36|
37|2. **`disk` is a free choice, and `local` is a valid target.** `config/filesystems.php:33-39` defines `local` alongside `public`, so `Storage::disk($request->disk)` accepts it.
38|
39|3. **`folder` is a free string**, so the destination path is not constrained to the `editor/` default.
40|
41|## Impact
42|
43|Any authenticated session reaches this endpoint, including the lowest-privilege role. The `auth` middleware requires a login; it does not require any permission, so a `viewer`-level account is sufficient.
44|
45|The consequence is a persistent, user-controlled object on a web-served disk with **no type or size constraint**, and the response hands back its URL. Because the handler passes `'public'` as the visibility argument and `config/filesystems.php:41-48` maps the `public` disk to `storage/app/public` with `'visibility' => 'public'`, the written file lands under the path that is exposed as `/storage/...`.
46|
47|This bypasses every upload rule the rest of this application enforces on itself. For contrast, the app's own upload paths validate both type and size:
48|
49|- `resources/views/livewire/tickets/⚡create.blade.php:96` — validates `mimes` and `max`
50|- `resources/views/livewire/tickets/⚡inbox.blade.php:677` — same
51|- `resources/views/livewire/hardware/import-hardware.blade.php:40` — same
52|
53|So the project has an upload policy, and this one route sits outside it.
54|
55|Severity is worth stating precisely rather than overstating. On this repo the web server's PHP handling is the only thing standing between an uploaded `.php`-named payload and execution — `public/storage` is not currently a symlinked directory in the working tree, and the `local` disk (`storage/app/private`) is served through a signature-checked route (`ServeFile::hasValidSignature()`, `vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Filesystem/ServeFile.php:55-61`). But that is an accident of current deployment configuration, not a control this application asserts. A deployment that runs `storage:link` — the standard Laravel step, referenced by no script or doc in this repo today — exposes the public disk directly.
56|
57|Two aggravating factors are independent of that:
58|
59|- `folder` is unconstrained, so writes are not confined to the intended `editor/` prefix.
60|- The route is **unused**. There is no `<x-editor>` / `<x-mary-editor>` usage anywhere in `resources/` or `app/` (grep returns 0 hits across the app). The endpoint is registered capability, not a feature anyone depends on.
61|
62|## Why this matters more than a typical missing-validation nit
63|
64|The gap is not that one handler forgot a rule. It is that the application's upload policy is enforced **per call site**, by hand, in each component that happens to handle a file. A route registered from a vendor package bypasses that policy entirely, because the policy lives in the callers rather than in the boundary. Any future package that registers an upload route has the same property.
65|
66|## Proposed fix
67|
68|Two acceptable directions; the first is preferable because the route is dead weight today.
69|
70|**Option A — remove the capability.** If `<x-editor>` is not planned, stop registering the package's routes rather than leaving a half-guarded write endpoint mounted at the app root. This can be done by not loading `vendor/robsontenorio/mary/routes/web.php` from the app's provider, so the app owns its route surface explicitly.
71|
72|**Option B — the app owns the contract.** Override the same URI from `routes/web.php` with a closure that re-declares the middleware and adds explicit validation before storing, e.g. `auth` plus a rule set constraining `file` to `required|file|mimes:jpg,jpeg,png,gif,webp|max:5120` and `disk` to an allow-list, deriving the folder server-side instead of accepting it from the request.
73|
74|Either way the fix is small and additive; the codebase already contains the exemplar pattern in its own upload call sites cited above.
75|
76|## Test plan
77|
78|- A feature test asserting `POST /mary/upload` returns 401/302 for a guest.
79|- A feature test asserting a non-permissioned authenticated user cannot write an arbitrary file (whatever Option A/B the implementer chooses).
80|- A regression test asserting no registered route writes to a request-selected disk without validation — cheap to express by asserting `POST /mary/upload` is absent (Option A) or rejects a disallowed mime (Option B).
81|
82|## Notes
83|
84|- Effort: S. Risk of the fix: LOW — nothing in `resources/` or `app/` calls this endpoint, so nothing legitimate breaks.

8|## مشکل
9|
10|`persons.n_code` یک فیلد کاملاً قابل‌نوشته‌دنده از دو مسیر است، ولی `hardwares.n_code` هیچ FK و هیچ cascade ندارد. نتیجه: یک تغییر ساده‌ی کد ملی، همه‌ی سخت‌افزارهای همان پرسنل را بی‌صدا یتیم می‌کند — دیتابیس هیچ خطا نمی‌دهد، هیچ لاگی نوشته نمی‌شود، و دارایی دیگر از هیچ مسیری در UI دیده نمی‌شود.
11|
12|### شواهد schema
13|
14|- `database/migrations/2025_03_20_000006_create_users_table.php:19-22` — `users.n_code` FK روی `persons.n_code` با `ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT`. یعنی تغییر کد ملی برای `users` **کاملاً درست و خودکار انجام می‌شود.**
15|- `database/migrations/2026_07_24_194955_create_hardwares_table.php:13,34` — `hardwares.n_code` فقط `string(10)` + `->index()`. **نه FK دارد نه cascade.**
16|- راستی‌آزمایی روی دیتابیس زنده: `pg_constraint` با `contype='f'` و `conrelid='hardwares'::regclass` → `[]` (هیچ FK روی جدول `hardwares` اصلاً وجود ندارد).
17|
18|### مسیرهای نوشتن
19|
20|| مسیر | محل |
21||---|---|
22|| `PUT /api/persons/{person}` | `routes/api.php:160` → `PersonController.php:118` (اعتبارسنجی `unique`) و `:132` (`$person->update($validated)`) |

24|| حذف پرسنل | `person.blade.php:120-141` — `catch` فقط خطای RESTRICT از سمت `users` را می‌گیرد. پیام خطا در `:139` («در جدول دیگری استفاده شده») عملاً فقط به `users` وفادار است؛ `hardwares` که FK ندارد یتیم می‌شود. |
25|
26|### اثرهای زنجیره‌ای (همه‌شان با `n_code` کلید خورده‌اند)
27|
28|- `app/Models/Hardware.php:120-122` — `belongsTo(Person::class, 'n_code', 'n_code')` → بعد از تغییر، `person` برابر `null` می‌شود.
29|- `resources/views/livewire/hardware/index.blade.php:50, 390, 451` — scope با `whereHas('person', fn ($q) => $q->whereIn('u_id', $accessibleIds))` ساخته می‌شود. یتیم → **هیچ واحدی دارایی را نمی‌بیند** (نه فقط واحد خارج از scope).
30|- همین فایل `:321`, `:345`, `:366` — `in_array($hw->person?->u_id, $accessibleIds)` → `null` → ویرایش، بازیابی و حذف برای **همه** رد می‌شود.
31|- `app/Http/Controllers/Api/HardwareController.php:116, 253, 284, 329` — `join('persons', 'hardwares.n_code', '=', 'persons.n_code')` از نوع inner است → ردیف از لیست، اکسپورت، آدیت‌تریل و سطل زباله خارج می‌شود.
32|- `app/Http/Controllers/Api/GisController.php:174, 345` — همان join → دارایی از نقشه و از شمارنده‌ی سخت‌افزار واحد حذف می‌شود.
33|- `app/Traits/HardwareIndexHelpers.php:62-64` — جست‌وجوی تاریخچه به `persons` join می‌زند؛ `! $unitId` → `history = []`. و `:240` (`nCodeInScope`) → `false` → rollback/restore هم رد می‌شود.

{"content": "1|### abharhit — 2026-10-10T12:39:35Z — id=6097582784
2|**Expert review — verified live on the current tree (Pest + dev-DB probes, commit `8fce3f8`). The defect is real and the failure chain is correct. Four numbers drifted, one claim is inverted, and the issue is missing an entire table from its FK list.**
3|
4|**Risk: HIGH — silent, one-click, unrecoverable org-tree wipe.** A single «حذف شد» toast detaches **178 staff**, deletes **178 `user_units` pivot rows**, orphans **219 hardware rows** so they become unreachable by *everyone including admins*, nulls **27 todos**, and deletes **396 GIS boundary rows**. Confirmed end-to-end by a Pest feature test run against the current tree (`tests/Feature/Tmp947ReproTest.php`, deleted after the run): after `deleteUnit` returns, `persons.u_id` is NULL, the pivot row count for that user is 0, the hardware row survives, and `HardwareAuditScope::unitIdForAudit()` returns NULL (deny-by-default) — for the deleting manager's own scope too. The «catch» never fires; the delete returns success.
5|
6|**Corrections to the issue:**
7|
8|1. **Every headline number is stale.** The issue's SQL is correct but the data has drifted: `units_deletable = 645` (issue: 648), `persons_stripped = 178` (issue: 154), `accounts_left_with_zero_scope = 178` (issue: 154), `hardware_rows = 219` (issue: 193), `todos_nulled = 27` (issue: 24). The severity claim is therefore **worse** than stated: 178/318 = **56%** of accounts, not 48%. All 178 affected accounts rely on `persons.u_id` alone — none retains a surviving `user_units` pivot. Re-run these at fix time; they will keep drifting.
9|2. **§2 has the recoverability backwards.** "Their account's unit assignment is deleted outright … re-linking is manual per person" is the *only recoverable* part of the cascade — a `user_units` row can simply be re-inserted. The unrecoverable one is `persons.u_id = NULL`, because the unit row it pointed at is gone; and while `persons.u_id` is nullable today, no writer in the app accepts a NULL (`person.blade.php:159` `'u_id' => 'required|exists:units,id'`, `PersonController.php:90/:125` `required`, `PersonImport.php:217-227` rejects empty), so an orphaned person is **un-editable through every surface** — that is what makes it unrecoverable, and it is the stronger point to make.
10|3. **`is_active` is not an unused column — it is already a live scope filter, and that changes the fix.** `Unit::recursiveDescendantQuery` (`app/Models/Unit.php:278-287`) filters `WHERE u.is_active = true` on every recursive step, so deactivating a unit already prunes it and its whole subtree from every org-scoped query. Measured on the dev DB: deactivating unit 4 (depth 3, 226 descendants) drops the visible tree for a base-1 user from **834 → 607**. So suggestion ② is not "the missing half of the feature" — the read side already honours the flag; **only the write side is missing** (`deleteUnit()`/`destroy()` are the sole writers; the only `is_active` toggler anywhere in the codebase is `it/zabbix-devices.blade.php:249-262`, which is exactly the template to copy).
11|4. **The FK table is incomplete — `boundaries` is missing and it is the least recoverable loss.** `units_boundary_fk` is `onDelete('cascade')` on `units.boundary_id` (`2025_03_20_000011_create_units_table.php:35-37`; `pg_constraint.confdeltype = 'c'`). Deleting a unit **deletes its boundary geometry**. 396 of the 645 deletable units carry a boundary and none is shared (`boundary shared by ≥2 units = 0`), so that loss is total and permanent — 396 polygons with no undo. The issue's table also omits `units_region_fk` (`restrict`) and `units_type_fk` (`no action`). The app already knows this FK is dangerous in the inverse direction: `units/map.blade.php:119-129` documents that deleting a `boundaries` row first would cascade-delete the unit and its children, and nulls `boundary_id` before the delete (#702). A unit delete is the same hazard pointed the other way.
12|5. **`RESTRICT` on `persons.u_id` (suggestion ③) is sound, and the schema supports it** — `persons.u_id` is nullable (`information_schema.is_nullable = YES` in both dev and test; migration `2026_09_03_002219` does `nullable()->change()` in `up()` and only restores `nullable(false)` in `down()`), so `persons_u_id_foreign_units`'s `confdeltype = 'n'` (SET NULL) fires. I confirmed both DBs are migrated and consistent (`migrate:status` shows both migrations ran). This is the single highest-leverage change: it converts 178 silent staff-strips into a raised error at the DB layer, below any guard the app might miss. Note it does **not** cover `user_units` cascade or the `boundaries` cascade, so it is necessary, not sufficient.
13|
14|**Root cause (confirmed):** the two guards match the two `restrict` FKs and nothing else. `resources/views/livewire/units/index.blade.php:380-385` (children) and `app/Http/Controllers/Api/UnitController.php:137-139` (children) are the **only** pre-delete checks; the `catch` at `:390-392` can only ever fire on `units_parent_fk` / `tickets_unit_fk`. Full FK census on `confrelid = 'units'`: `units_parent_fk` r, `tickets_unit_fk` r, `units_region_fk` r *(unguarded, unlisted)*, `units_boundary_fk` c, `uu_unit_fk` c, and SET NULL on `persons` / `todos` / `task_activities` (`to_unit_id`) / `maintenance_schedules` / `daily_reports`. Six of the eight unit FKs cascade or null silently; the issue counted eight, the real number including `boundaries` and `regions` is ten.
15|
16|**Recommended plan (M):**
17|1. **Settle the FK direction first** (correction 5) — migrate `persons_u_id_foreign_units` to `onDelete('restrict')`. Cheapest, app-independent, fails loudly. Deliberate decision, documented blast radius: `persons.u_id` must then never be set NULL by any writer, which the current validation rules already guarantee.
18|2. **Add a deactivate action instead of making delete the retire path** (correction 3). `deactivateUnit()` on `units.index` + `UnitController`, mirroring `zabbix-devices.blade.php:249-262`, wired to `is_active` (already fillable on `Unit`, defaults `true`, already honoured by the scope CTE and by `TicketTargetUnit.php:49`, `users/index.blade.php:71`, `tickets/inbox.blade.php:82`). `Unit::updated()` already invalidates `unit_hierarchy` (`AppServiceProvider.php:107`).
19|3. **Refuse deletes that would orphan anything.** In both entry points, before `delete()`: `persons()->exists()`, `user_units()->exists()`, `todos()->exists()`, `maintenance_schedules()->exists()`, `task_activities()->exists()`, `daily_reports()->exists()`, and `boundary_id !== null` — each reported with a count. If `boundary_id` is set, say the polygon is destroyed too.
20|4. **Fix the misleading toast** at `:390-392`: «امکان حذف وجود ندارد زیرا در جدول دیگری استفاده شده است» implies the cascade tables are protected. They are the opposite — they are precisely the ones that succeed.
21|5. **API parity.** `UnitController::destroy()` (`:129-147`) is strictly weaker than the UI path *and* has no `try/catch`: the `tickets` restrict surfaces as an uncaught **500**, not a 422 — `bootstrap/app.php:80-124` renders only `NotFoundHttpException` and `ModelNotFoundException`, so `QueryException` is unhandled. It needs the same guard set plus a proper 422.
22|6. **Tests**, next to `test_delete_unit` (`tests/Feature/UnitsIndexLivewireTest.php:398-416`) and `test_delete_fk_blocked` (`:549-566`): a unit with a person + hardware refuses the delete and both rows survive; **an empty unit still deletes** (happy path — my repro confirms it passes on the current tree, so this guards against the fix over-reaching); a unit with a boundary refuses and the geometry survives; an account whose only unit is deleted ends with empty scope and unreachable hardware (pin whichever contract you choose); `DELETE /api/units/{unit}` on a unit with tickets returns 422, not 500; and a `persons_u_id_foreign_units` delete raises at the DB layer once it is `restrict`.
23|
24|**Not verified:** no browser run — `scripts/e2e-test.sh` was not executed (off-limits for a review), so the cascade was verified at the constraint catalog, data-probe, and Pest-feature-test layers, not through a live UI click. The issue's 154 / 193 / 24 / 648 figures were not reproduced at any point; the DB has drifted since they were measured. `task_activities`, `daily_reports` and `maintenance_schedules` currently hold **0** rows referencing a deletable unit, so their blast radius today is zero — the count is the mechanism, not the data. I did not exercise `UnitController::destroy()` end-to-end through a real Sanctum token; the 500-vs-422 claim is read from `bootstrap/app.php` plus the absence of any `try/catch` in the method.
25|
26|**Related, do not duplicate:** #876 (`maintenance_schedules` half of this same cascade), #862 (`n_code`-rename writer, identical downstream failure mode), #817 (org-scope on these buttons — closed/fixed).
27|
28|*Status: still present on `8fce3f8`. `git log -S 'persons_u_id_foreign_units'` returns only `50012e4` ("feat: add FK constraint on persons.u_id to units.id", Plan 014) and the `down()` path of `2026_09_03_002219`; nothing has changed the delete path's guards.*
29|
30|*Size: M — one migration + two guarded entry points + one new deactivate action + 5–6 tests. The FK direction (step 1) is the only product decision.*

text.description: The text to convert to speech. Provider-specific per-request character caps apply automatically (OpenAI 4096, xAI 15000, MiniMax 10000, ElevenLabs 5k-40k depending on model); longer input is split into ordered chunks without silent truncation.

output_path.description: Optional custom file path to save the audio. Defaults to ~/.hermes/audio_cache/<timestamp>.mp3

speed.description: Playback speed multiplier. 1.0 = normal, 0.5 = very slow (language learning), 2.0 = fast. Range: 0.25-4.0. Overrides the speed configured in config.yaml.

instructions.description: Optional voice-design guidance: tone, emotion, pacing, accent, whispering, impressions (e.g. 'Speak in a cheerful, excited whisper'). Forwarded to the OpenAI backend (gpt-4o-mini-tts and OpenAI-compatible voice-design servers). Silently ignored by backends that don't support it.

function.name: vision_analyze
function.description: Load an image into the conversation so you can see it. Call it any time the user references an image — then answer from what you see.

image_url.description: Image URL (http/https), local file path, or data: URL to load.

question.description: Your question or request about the image.

region.description: Optional [x1, y1, x2, y2] crop in ORIGINAL-image pixel coordinates, applied before any downscaling — the crop keeps full resolution. Load the full image first, then re-call with a region to zoom into small text or fine detail.

function.name: web_extract
function.description: Extract content from web page URLs. Returns clean page content in markdown/text (no LLM summarization — fast). Also works with PDF URLs (arxiv papers, documents) — pass the PDF link directly. Pages within the char budget (default 15000) return whole; larger pages return a head+tail window with a footer telling you the full text's saved file path and the read_file call to page through the omitted middle. Inline images appear as [IMAGE: alt] placeholders; real image URLs are kept as links. If a URL fails or times out, use the browser tool instead.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from (max 5 URLs per call)

char_limit.description: Optional per-page character budget sent back (default 15000). Pages larger than this are head+tail truncated with the full text stored to disk. Raise it when you need more of a long page inline.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for information. Returns up to 5 results by default with titles, URLs, and descriptions. The query is passed through to the configured backend, so operators such as site:domain, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, and "exact phrase" may work when the backend supports them.

query.description: The search query to look up on the web. You may include backend-supported operators such as site:example.com, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, or "exact phrase".

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits. For an EXISTING file, call read_file first: write_file refuses (file untouched) when this task has no current full read/write of the file or the file changed on disk since; on refusal, read_file, merge, then retry. Auto-runs syntax checks on .py/.json/.yaml/.toml and other linted languages; only NEW errors introduced by this write are surfaced (pre-existing errors are filtered out). The result's verified:true means the on-disk content hash was confirmed — do NOT re-read the file to check the write landed.

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file

function.name: tool_search
function.description:
Search 52 additional tools that are loaded on demand. Takes a list of queries searched in parallel against the same catalog; send one query per distinct capability you need. Queries are keyword searches, not questions: the app or service name plus an action and object, no filler words (`gmail send email`, `nvidia driver status`, not `what's my GPU driver version?`); a word no tool contains makes the query return nothing. Returns matching tool names grouped per query plus a shared map with each tool's description. Follow with `tool_describe` to load full parameter schemas, then `tool_call` to invoke. Tools listed at the top of this system prompt are already available and do not need to be searched.
